sections_target.text: This document sets out the steps for fitting dead-end joints for AAAC alloy conductors on overhead lines using the hydraulic press instead of the parallel clamps used in welding the conductors.

The document was reviewed by the general managers of overhead lines in the regions of the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company and the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.

rows: A work order must be issued including the names of the workers, and they must have occupational safety and health category cards.
Occupational safety and health equipment must be used, such as a safety helmet, safety shoes, cotton overalls, etc.
Joints are prohibited at the following crossings: above railways, the River Nile, navigable canals, main roads, electricity and telephone lines, etc.

Do not load the weight of the conductor on the sleeve (joint/ferrule) during each compression, to ensure the joint stays straight and does not bend, especially when making the first compression; in general the conductor and the joint shall be horizontal and in one straight line during compression.
Comply with the manufacturer's instructions regarding the number of compressions and the distances between them.
Occupational safety and health equipment such as protective goggles, safety helmet, cotton overalls, etc.
A suitable compression press for the joints and the dies suitable for the joint section and type, as per the manufacturer's recommendation.
Hacksaw, adhesive tape, suitable solvent, cloth, cloth sandpaper, metal brush with steel wire 0.2 to 0.3 mm long.
A special file for removing and chamfering excess material, protrusions or joint burrs and smoothing them.
Make sure the die represents the correct size.
Make sure the ends and joints are clean.
Make sure the conductor end is sound; if there is damage, cut off the damaged part.

Clean all parts of the conductor strands to be compressed, especially for greased conductors or old conductors; in the first case use a suitable solvent, and in the other case use cloth sandpaper or a metal brush 0.2 to 0.3 mm long.

Put a reference mark on the conductor at a distance equal to the length of the inner cavity of the conductor end, then insert the conductor into the end and let it slide in until it reaches the mark (Figure x1a), taking into account the lay direction of the conductor.
Insert the aluminium dead-end joint with the steel dead-end joint and compress the steel end first — eye end hole.

Compress the end starting from the side near the terminal end (Figure x1b), then continue compressing the conductor until they overlap (over lap), taking into account the direction of the two bridle lugs in the correct direction.
Clean carefully, as shown in step (4), all the wires at the end of the conductor (the bridle).
Insert the conductor into the end of the joint (the bridle lug), then start compression from the terminal end side (Figure x1c) and continue as per the previous instructions.
Clean well the contact surface of the terminal end and the joint with cloth, then tie the two ends together.

Introduction
This document sets out the steps for fitting dead-end joints for AAAC alloy conductors on overhead lines using the hydraulic press instead of the parallel clamps used in welding the conductors.
The document was reviewed by the general managers of overhead lines in the regions of the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company and the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.
Safety Precautions

Occupational safety and health equipment must be used, such as a safety helmet, safety shoes, cotton overalls, etc. | 
The following shall be observed:
Joints are prohibited at the following crossings: above railways, the River Nile, navigable canals, main roads, electricity and telephone lines, etc. | 
Do not load the weight of the conductor on the sleeve (joint/ferrule) during each compression, to ensure the joint stays straight and does not bend, especially when making the first compression; in general the conductor and the joint shall be horizontal and in one straight line during compression. | 
Comply with the manufacturer's instructions regarding the number of compressions and the distances between them. |

A special file for removing and chamfering excess material, protrusions or joint burrs and smoothing them. | 
Procedures to be Carried Out

Insert the aluminium dead-end joint with the steel dead-end joint and compress the steel end first — eye end hole. | 6.
Compress the end starting from the side near the terminal end (Figure x1b), then continue compressing the conductor until they overlap (over lap), taking into account the direction of the two bridle lugs in the correct direction. | 7.
Clean carefully, as shown in step (4), all the wires at the end of the conductor (the bridle). | 8.
Insert the conductor into the end of the joint (the bridle lug), then start compression from the terminal end side (Figure x1c) and continue as per the previous instructions. | 9.
